english: The value of the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n(n+1)}{3^{n+1}}=\frac{2}{3^2}+\frac{6}{3^3}+\frac{12}{3^4}+\frac{20}{3^5}+\cdots$ is ______.
solution: Numerators $2,6,12,20,\dots$ have differences $4,6,8,\dots$ (an AP), so one subtraction gives an AGP
solution_full: Let $S=\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)}{3^{n+1}}$; it converges (ratio test with ratio $\frac13$).

Subtracting term by term: $S-\dfrac S3=\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n(n+1)-(n-1)n}{3^{n+1}}=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2n}{3^{n+1}}$, since the numerators $2,6,12,20,\dots$ have differences $4,6,8,\dots=2(n)$, an arithmetic progression. The new series is arithmetico-geometric.
originality_note: New: a series with quadratic numerators n(n + 1) over a GP is reduced to an AGP by one shift-and-subtract step, because the numerators have differences in AP (way 5: method of differences converting to an AGP). Closest known: 'sum n^2 x^n' by differentiation. Different because: the numerators are pronic numbers written out as 2, 6, 12, 20, and the intended route is the shift-and-subtract conversion, not a memorised formula.

concept_use.Sequences convertible to AGP: Shifting by one place and subtracting converts the quadratic-numerator series into the AGP sum 2n/3^{n+1}, which is then summed by the same trick.
